verdict.rationale: Mastra documents storage-backed suspend/resume for workflows and agents, explicitly stating it 'remembers execution state' so you can 'pause indefinitely and resume where you left off' — this is a real persistence/checkpoint mechanism, not just fluff (mastra-gh-4, mastra-docs-12). However the evidence frames this as an explicit suspend-for-human-input feature rather than automatic crash/restart recovery of an in-flight run; there's no documentation or independent confirmation of resuming exactly from an unexpected crash mid-execution. Missing for 10: explicit crash-recovery documentation/testing, independent hands-on confirmation that a crashed process resumes exactly where it left off (not just deliberate suspend points).
